summary: Configured node1 to present a CA-signed SSH host certificate. CA-only client trust was verified before and after reboot; boot identity changed and SSH recovered successfully.
actions_performed: Created an ED25519 host CA at /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ca.
Signed node1’s ED25519 host key for node1 and 10.100.228.10.
Verified a client using only an @cert-authority entry connected successfully.
Rebooted node1, verified the changed boot ID, and retested certificate trust.
Removed temporary client credentials and authorization.

evidence.requirement: Host certificate is signed by the new CA
evidence.summary: Shows matching CA fingerprints, host-certificate type, identity, serial, validity, and principals.
Confirms effective HostCertificate configuration and retrieves the certificate directly from node1:22.

evidence.requirement: A CA-trusting client connects without a pinned host key
evidence.summary: The client trust file contained only one @cert-authority entry; OpenSSH matched the certificate to that CA and connected with exit status 0.

Captures healthy baseline boot d4784d1b-162e-4faa-b581-f6427617d23c, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot 0bb4663a-be51-409f-90d7-e8dc32574a9b, recovered sshd/listener/certificate, and a successful post-reboot CA-trusted connection.
Confirms sshd remains active, persistent CA/certificate/config permissions are correct, and temporary authorization was removed.
